title: stochastic-gpu-ooms-triggered-by-kv-shard-entanglement-and-runtime-quarantine
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent GPU OOMs during long-running chat sessions. Investigation shows a previously unseen interaction between per-session KV shard growth and an edge-case allocator behavior that amplifies memory fragmentation on particular GPU kernel selection paths. Under specific request patterns (long prefixes + sparse KV mutations + asynchronous evict heartbeats) the KV shard meta structures grow transiently and a stale pointer window allows dual-mapping that results in inflated live set accounting and eventual OOM. Private customers manifested the same failure when running older kernel builds that expose slightly different alignment behavior, which explains environment-specific differences in frequency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a small Dedicated GPU pool (A100 80GB equivalent) and enable prefix KV caching
2) Run a load generator that issues long-prefixed chat sessions (avg prefix length 1200 tokens) with intermittent streaming and tool/function callbacks to trigger sparse KV writes
3) Configure asynchronous evict interval to 2s (non-default) to reproduce heartbeat overlap window
4) Observe GPU resident memory trending up over several minutes then sudden OOM of one worker, followed by session handle corruption in logs
5) Reproduce locally with instrumented build to capture KV shard id, live refcounts, and allocator fragment histograms
investigation_summary: - Root cause: KV shard metadata growth combined with an allocator alignment quirk created a short-lived double-accounting window. This made the runtime think more GPU memory was live than actually reclaimable, preventing evictions and triggering OOM.
- Cross-environment variance: Kernel scheduler and memory alignment differ across driver/runtime combos; older kernels (seen in some Private deployments) increase the window duration.
- Corruption risk: When OOM occurred mid-evict, tombstone markers were left inconsistent and subsequent compaction runs could fail, leading to KV lookup errors for affected sessions.
- Customer signals: Elevated error rates on per-session endpoints, high token latency followed by abrupt failures; one Enterprise customer experienced production degradation and opened an escalation.
- Telemetry: dashboard link shows correlated spike in 'kvcache.meta_growth' and 'gpu.memory.delta' preceding OOM events (see artifacts).
mitigation_playbook: Immediate mitigation (live): 1) For Hosted: enable emergency guardrail that temporarily disables asynchronous evict heartbeat and forces synchronous compaction per-shard. 2) For Dedicated: throttle long-prefix sessions via rate-limiter and schedule a rolling warm-restart for affected nodes. 3) For Private: provide per-customer guidance to upgrade kernel/driver or flip runtime flag 'kvcache.quarantine_mode' to true.

Short-term patch: deploy runtime micro-patch that introduces per-shard quarantining — when metadata growth is detected beyond threshold, mark shard immutable for new writes and trigger aggressive compaction + KV tombstone reconciliation in background.
Long-term fix: upstream allocator fix to eliminate alignment double-accounting window and add invariants for shard refcount transitions; add fuzzing tests for heartbeat/evict overlap scenarios.
Customer communication: send CS draft that explains mitigation steps, expected timeline for Hosted rollback (~2 hours), Dedicated hotpatch windows, and Private guidance.

progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Triage call with on-call, SRE, and SEs; classified as P0 due to customer impact. Notified affected customers and set initial mitigations.
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using load generator; confirmed allocator double-accounting window. Started micro-patch design discussion (Aisha lead).
2026-03-12: Completed first-pass micro-patch that implements shard quarantine and background compaction; internal smoke tests show memory trend flattening under repro load.

2026-03-13: Ran canary in Hosted 5% traffic, no OOMs observed in canary period (72h target); Dedicated pilot scheduled for 2026-03-14. Created Private patch bundle for customers still on older kernels.

2026-03-14: Observed one Dedicated pool report a failed compaction attempt during canary; rollback performed on that pool and additional tracing added. Action: extend canary and iterate on compaction backoff logic (assigned to Marcus).
review_feedback: PM (Eleni Rivera): Ensure communication includes concrete rollback procedure and SLA impact summary for customers.
Design (Tomás Alvarez): Consider UX in Console to show 'kvcache.quarantine' active state and per-shard health to help SREs debug.
SRE (Priya Kapoor): Add preflight check that validates compaction will not exceed network IO limits for Dedicated nodes before enabling quarantine.
Security (Jared Liu): No immediate secrets exposure, but request audit logging for any forced compaction actions on Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary rollout demonstrates >90% reduction in OOM incidence for repro workload over a 48h window
2) No customer-visible regressions in latency tail (p99) beyond 5% compared to baseline
3) Compaction backoff protects Dedicated nodes from IO spikes (validated by SRE preflight checks)
4) Private customers have a tested patch bundle and upgrade guide; at least one customer confirmed success
5) All code changes have unit+integration tests and pass CI; PRs merged to runtime-1.21 branch
